title: When the Current Sings
premise: Jude Okafor, a railroad engineer who fled his family's legacy by mapping abandoned mountain lines, is pulled back into the world when the survey expedition he quietly supplied goes silent upriver. Joining a ragged rescue party—a disgraced medic, a runaway radio operator, and the expedition leader's estranged daughter, Mara—Jude must cross the Kestrel Range before early snows seal the passes. Along the way he learns the expedition vanished because its leader found a live ore vein the railway consortium will kill to control, and that his own map was the reason they could reach it. At the climax, Jude must choose between destroying his life's work to bury the route forever or saving it to save Mara's life when she falls through a collapsed trestle; he chooses her, burning the map and carrying her down through the first snow. They return as strangers to their old lives but a family to each other, and the mountain keeps its silence.
about_author: Vesper Almeida is the pen name of a former field cartographer who spent a decade surveying decommissioned rail lines across three continents before turning to fiction. They write from a cabin with no road access, reachable only by the last working freight spur in the valley.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Establishes his hermit-like routine maintaining closed rail lines and his ritual of measuring life in miles walked. A supply drop for an upriver survey expedition is his only human contact. Emotional beat: comfortable isolation shown as a wound in disguise, cracked when the expedition's scheduled radio check comes back static.

chapters.title: Static on the Kestrel Line
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He reports the silence and is shocked when the consortium sends a search party—and insists he come, since only he knows the old trestle routes. He refuses; then finds the expedition leader's final transmission was addressed to him by name. Emotional beat: the past knocking, guilt overriding fear as he packs his map.

chapters.title: The Company of Strangers
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, introducing the rescue party at the riverhead: Ruth, a medic struck off the registry; Pip, a teenage radio operator who stowed away; and Mara Voss, the expedition leader's daughter, who blames Jude's maps for her father's obsession. Emotional beat: friction and distrust, the found family assembling in miniature.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The party follows the river gorge, finding the expedition's abandoned cache and a journal hinting her father found something in the range worth hiding. Mara confronts Jude about his maps; he deflects. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into purpose, and Mara beginning to read Jude more clearly than he'd like.

chapters.title: The Trestle at Wolf's Tooth
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A storm forces them onto a rotting viaduct Jude last inspected five years ago; Pip nearly dies when a span gives way, saved by Ruth's skill and Jude's knowledge. Emotional beat: the first bonds of trust, forged in terror, and Jude realizing he cares about these people whether he wants to or not.

chapters.title: Snowline
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. They find the first body and evidence the expedition split—one faction wanted to sell the ore find, the other wanted to bury it. Mara's father's journal reveals he trusted 'the engineer who erased the lines'—Jude. Emotional beat: betrayal and revelation; Mara's anger pivots from Jude to the consortium men trailing them.

chapters.title: The Men from the Consortium
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The search party behind them isn't a rescue—it's a cleanup crew. A night confrontation at a fire lookout leaves Pip captured and Jude forced to bargain with his map as ransom. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal; Jude chooses the group over his life's work for the first time.

chapters.title: The Pass Called Mercy
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A brutal climb through the high pass to intercept the crew at the expedition's last camp, where they find her father alive but dying, having rigged the mine entrance to collapse. His last words to Jude: 'You always knew where to bury things.' Emotional beat: reconciliation, grief, and the ticking clock of the coming snows.

chapters.title: What We Bury
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The climax: Jude triggers the collapse that seals the ore vein and the route, but Mara falls through a failing trestle into the gorge. Jude goes down after her, burning his final copy of the map to signal the consortium crew away while he climbs with her on his back through the first snowfall. Emotional beat: love against duty, decided in a single breath.

chapters.title: The Last Mile
chapters.summary: Alternating Jude and Mara POV. The survivors descend as the passes close behind them; the consortium's claims die with the route. In the valley town, Ruth reopens a practice, Pip finds a family, and Jude, mapless for the first time, asks Mara to walk with him into a future he can't measure. Emotional beat: found family solidified; the current finally sings instead of silences.
